correctness.rationale: An independent sharp bound avoids the frozen minimax step. Write a=(1+t)/2, b=1/n, u=|t|, q=a+b+2u. Hub-antisymmetric and leaf-contrast eigenvalues of M are nonnegative; the remaining block is congruent to [[a,t],[t,b]]. Thus M is positive exactly when kappa=t^2-ab<=0, giving the two stated roots and norm one in that region. Otherwise set d=kappa/q and V=d vv*, where v has entry 1 at each hub and -sgn(t) at each leaf. The corresponding block of M+V is congruent to [[a+d,t-sgn(t)d],[t-sgn(t)d,b+d]], with determinant zero and nonnegative diagonal. Elementary contrast eigenvalues are unchanged. Thus M=(M+V)-V is a difference of positive kernels. Combining their Gram factors with a sign on the second summand bounds the ordinary and all amplified norms by the common sum of their diagonals, 1+2d. For p proportional within the two classes as stated, let s be its hub mass. On the compressed constant plane, D_p V D_p has range spanned by (sqrt(s),-sgn(t)sqrt(1-s)); the range of D_p(M+V)D_p there is spanned by ((a+u)sqrt(s),sgn(t)(b+u)sqrt(1-s)). These are orthogonal at s=(b+u)/q. D_p V D_p then has its sole nonzero eigenvalue d on the negative line of D_p M D_p, which has trace one. The spectral-sign input gives the lower bound 1+2d, including degenerate contrast eigenvalues. Positivity and norm endpoints simplify as stated. For the infinite case, b tends to zero; finite compressions give the lower bound. Taking d=t^2/(a+2u) for t nonzero yields the same positive-kernel construction on every finite corner (remaining determinant b(a+d)>=0), with bounded Gram vectors, hence a normal completely bounded multiplier. At t=0 the multiplier is the diagonal expectation. This proves all operator, cb and limiting claims in the specified parameter range.
residual_risks: The proof relies on real weights in [-1,1] for positivity on both contrast spaces. Numerical trace-norm tests are not needed for the exact bound.
